components.title: AWS Secrets Manager (SPARC Application Secrets)
components.description: Secrets Manager secrets providing credential isolation between services. SPARC application secrets (app-secrets) and Heimdall security visualization secrets (heimdall-credentials) are stored separately with independent OAuth credentials, JWT secrets, and admin passwords including auto-generated SECRET_KEY_BASE, authentication settings (OIDC, LDAP), SMTP credentials, and operational parameters. Deployed via Terraform (AWS/ECS/modules/secrets/). <!-- UPDATE: Insert secret ARN and name for your deployment. -->

control-implementations.description: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 control implementations for application secrets management

implemented-requirements.description: Authenticator Management: SECRET_KEY_BASE is auto-generated as a 128-character random string via Terraform random_password — it is never manually set or stored in configuration files. OIDC client secrets, LDAP bind passwords, and SMTP passwords are stored in Secrets Manager rather than in environment variables, tfvars files, or source code. All secrets are encrypted at rest with AWS KMS. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000175. Heimdall Server has its own credential store (heimdall-credentials) with independent JWT secret, admin password, OIDC client secret, and GitHub OAuth secret — credential compromise in one service does not expose the other.

Protection of Information at Rest: All application secrets are encrypted at rest using AWS KMS within Secrets Manager. This includes SECRET_KEY_BASE, OIDC client secrets, LDAP bind password, and SMTP password. Secrets are never written to disk in plaintext — they are injected into ECS tasks at runtime via the Secrets Manager integration. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000231.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Secrets Manager uses AES-256 encryption via KMS. Consider using a customer-managed KMS key for additional control over encryption key lifecycle.

implemented-requirements.description: Access Enforcement: Access to application secrets is restricted to the ECS task execution role via a resource-level IAM policy granting only secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on the specific secret ARN. No other IAM principals have access. The secret is not accessible from the console without explicit IAM permissions. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000033.
implemented-requirements.remarks: IAM policy in the iam module restricts access to both db_secret_arn and app_secret_arn specifically.

implemented-requirements.description: Identification and Authentication: The secrets module manages authentication configuration for multiple identity providers: local login (username/password with configurable password expiry), OIDC/OAuth2 (Okta, Entra ID, Keycloak, Auth0), and LDAP. MFA can be enforced via OIDC provider (SPARC_OIDC_FORCE_MFA). Session timeout is configurable (SPARC_SESSION_TIMEOUT_MINUTES). Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000148.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Authentication method selection is controlled by SPARC_ENABLE_LOCAL_LOGIN, SPARC_ENABLE_OIDC, and SPARC_ENABLE_LDAP flags.

implemented-requirements.description: Account Management: Application-level account management is configured via secrets: user self-registration (SPARC_ENABLE_USER_REGISTRATION), auto-deactivation after inactivity (SPARC_INACTIVITY_DAYS), and password expiry (SPARC_PASSWORD_EXPIRY_DAYS). These settings enforce organizational account lifecycle policies within the SPARC application. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000023.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Default: registration disabled, 30-day inactivity timeout, 30-day password expiry. Configurable via Terraform variables.

implemented-requirements.description: Event Logging: Secrets Manager logs all secret access events (GetSecretValue) to AWS CloudTrail, providing an audit trail of when secrets were retrieved and by which IAM principal. Application logging configuration (SPARC_LOG_LEVEL, SPARC_STRUCTURED_LOGGING) is managed here, enabling structured JSON output for CloudWatch/SIEM integration. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000089.
implemented-requirements.remarks: CloudTrail records all Secrets Manager API calls. SPARC_STRUCTURED_LOGGING=true enables JSON log format for automated log analysis.

implemented-requirements.description: Authenticator Management — Periodic Rotation (#151): The admin break-glass password ({prefix}/admin-credentials.sparc_admin_password) is rotated automatically every var.admin_rotation_period_days (default 30) by a dedicated Lambda function. The Lambda implements the AWS Secrets Manager 4-step rotation protocol (createSecret/setSecret/testSecret/finishSecret) on top of SPARC's POST /api/admin/refresh_credentials endpoint. SigV4 signing uses the Lambda's IAM role identity — no static credentials in the rotation path. Failure path is rollback-by-omission: AWSPENDING is left in place, AWSCURRENT unchanged, consumers continue to read the prior password. SPARC_HASH (per-instance master secret for SparcKeyDerivation) and SECRET_KEY_BASE rotate on independent cadences. Reference: NIST SP 800-53 IA-5, IA-5(1), IA-5(1)(d), DISA SRG-APP-000164.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Terraform: aws_lambda_function.admin_rotation + aws_secretsmanager_secret_rotation.admin (both in modules/lambda/main.tf). Gated on var.enable_admin_rotation. Rotation requires SPARC #403 endpoint to be live. AWS Config rule secretsmanager-rotation-enabled-check passes when enabled.

implemented-requirements.description: Account Management — Automated System Account Management (#151): Admin credential rotation is fully automated via EventBridge-driven Lambda invocation through Secrets Manager's native rotation protocol. No human action is required for routine rotation; manual force-rotation is available via aws secretsmanager rotate-secret for incident response. Reference: NIST SP 800-53 AC-2(1).
implemented-requirements.remarks: Lambda has reserved_concurrent_executions=1 to serialize rotations. SQS DLQ captures invocation-level failures; SNS publish on rotation-step failure provides operator visibility.

implemented-requirements.description: Cryptographic Key Establishment — SPARC_HASH master secret (#195): A per-instance master secret, generated as a 64-char cryptographically random value via Terraform random_password and stored in a dedicated Secrets Manager entry ({prefix}/SPARC_HASH). Encrypted at rest with a customer-managed KMS key. Used as the HKDF input to SparcKeyDerivation for purpose-specific symmetric keys (federation peer credentials, future per-purpose subsystem keys). Independent of SECRET_KEY_BASE so rotation cadences and audit trails stay separate. Reference: NIST SP 800-53 SC-12.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Terraform: aws_secretsmanager_secret.sparc_hash with kms_key_id from the secrets CMK. Plain-string secret value; ECS execution role granted GetSecretValue on this ARN explicitly.

implemented-requirements.description: Cryptographic Protection — Customer-Managed KMS for SPARC_HASH (#195): The SPARC_HASH secret is encrypted at rest with a customer-managed KMS key (not the AWS-managed default). All KMS Decrypt operations are audited via CloudTrail. Reference: NIST SP 800-53 SC-13.
implemented-requirements.remarks: kms_key_id = var.kms_key_arn passed through from the secrets module; same CMK used for app-secrets and admin-credentials.

implemented-requirements.description: Authenticator Management — SPARC_HASH Lifecycle (#195): The master secret is provisioned externally to SPARC, distinct from secret_key_base, and can be rotated independently. Rotation requires re-encryption of dependent rows (federation peer credentials encrypted with HKDF-derived keys); coordination with SPARC's sparc:reencrypt:rotate_master_key rake task is documented in docs/dev/admin_rotation.md. Reference: NIST SP 800-53 IA-5.
implemented-requirements.remarks: lifecycle { ignore_changes = [secret_string] } on the SPARC_HASH version resource so post-rotation drift doesn't trigger Terraform rollback.

implemented-requirements.description: Access Enforcement — Write-Only Task Role on admin-credentials (#197): The SPARC ECS task role has secretsmanager:PutSecretValue + secretsmanager:UpdateSecretVersionStage on the admin-credentials ARN, but explicitly does NOT have secretsmanager:GetSecretValue. SPARC_ADMIN_PASSWORD is delivered to the running container via task-definition secrets[] injection (read by the ECS execution role at task launch); the task role itself can only OVERWRITE the secret, never read it via SDK. A compromised SPARC task can rotate the admin password (loud, ops-detectable) but cannot exfiltrate the current value. Reference: NIST SP 800-53 AC-3, DISA SRG-APP-000033.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Terraform: aws_iam_role_policy.task_admin_write_only in modules/iam/main.tf. The task-def secrets[] block in ecs_fargate/main.tf delivers SPARC_ADMIN_PASSWORD via the execution role's GetSecretValue grant on admin-credentials.

implemented-requirements.description: Authenticator Management — Rotation Lambda Bearer Token (#197): The admin-rotation Lambda authenticates to SPARC's POST /api/admin/refresh_credentials with a sparc_sa_* service-account Bearer token stored in a dedicated Secrets Manager entry ({prefix}/rotation-lambda-token). Token is fetched on each invocation; SPARC's side validates against the bound service account's allow-list. No SigV4 verification middleware required on SPARC's side. The token secret is operator-populated post-apply via aws secretsmanager put-secret-value; never lives in Terraform state. Reference: NIST SP 800-53 IA-5.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Lambda IAM role has GetSecretValue on this single secret ARN only. Token rotation on SPARC's side takes effect on the next Lambda invocation without redeployment.
